title: Refuse Inclusion.model_construct, like Mention, Claim, CaseResult, and Example
description: Inclusion (src/amber/schemas/evidence.py) checks the private minting context in a validator but does not override model_construct, which skips validators, so Inclusion.model_construct(...) yields an unverified Inclusion. Mention, Claim, CaseResult, and Example all override it to raise. Graph registration re-grounds spans, which limits the damage, but ADR 0003 (only grounding mints spans) should hold at construction. Add the override and adversarial tests for plain construction, model_validate without the context, and model_construct (tests/test_invariants.py). Tightened validation: classify with the contract-change skill (breaking for any caller using model_construct; none in this repository). Found by the reviewer fact-checking ADR 0003 (amber-7q0.2).
acceptance_criteria: Inclusion.model_construct raises TypeError; a test tries each bypass and failed before the change; contract-change classification approved.
close_reason: Inclusion.model_construct (and deprecated construct) raise TypeError; test_inclusion_refuses_every_bypass_of_grounding failed before the fix. Contract-change classification (breaking, Python API only; no schema_version bump; migration note) approved by Will Thompson. Reviewer PASS; model_copy(update=...) gap filed as amber-8gm.

title: Make targets, hooks, and CI for quality
description: Wire the existing quality checks into the workflow (scope narrowed by Will Thompson, 2026-11-09): make quality-fast (lint, lint-imports, ratchet), make quality (quality-fast; slower checks join it as they land), make check includes quality; CI's tests job runs make quality with full history and the ratchet writes its report to the job summary; post_edit runs lint-imports for src/ edits; the stop hook adds make imports and make ratchet. vulture/duplication (.6), deptry and the dependency gate with its label (.7), diff-coverage (.8), and the diff budget with its label (.9) wire themselves into make quality, make check, and CI when they land. The stop hook's ~90 s budget is amber-7q0.18.
acceptance_criteria: make check and CI run make quality; the hooks run the new commands (tests/test_agent_hooks.py); the new targets add only seconds to the stop hook (measured).

title: quality/ratchet.py: violation counts that may not increase
description: Collect per-metric counts: ruff violations per rule code (exit-zero JSON), mypy --strict errors in src/, vulture findings, duplicate-code blocks, noqa / type: ignore / pragma: no cover counts, unjustified suppressions (no trailing justification; tolerance 0), max cyclomatic complexity per module (radon), import-linter ignore_imports entries. Compare with quality/baseline.json: exit 2 on any increase, printing old -> new and the new violations (file:line:code); files added relative to origin/main must have zero ruff, mypy-strict, vulture, and unjustified-suppression findings; decreases print 'ratchet can be tightened'. make quality-rebaseline writes the baseline only with ALLOW_ORACLE_CHANGE=1 and refuses if anything increased. Protected: quality/. Standard library plus the tools' JSON outputs; tool versions pinned in the dev extra (dependency change: human approval).
acceptance_criteria: Each spec 11 ratchet check passes: new violation in an existing file fails with old->new and file:line; unjustified noqa fails; complexity > 10 in a new file fails; a fixed violation prints the tighten message; rebaseline refuses to loosen.
close_reason: Ratchet merged in #43 (da0e8d2) with the human-generated baseline (27 metrics); make ratchet prints ratchet ok on main. Spec 11 ratchet criteria covered by tests/test_ratchet.py (70 tests, each rule mutation-checked). Reviewer PASS after one FAIL round; leftovers amber-7q0.16.

description: Move [tool.ruff] and [tool.importlinter] out of pyproject.toml into ruff.toml and .importlinter with identical behavior (no rule changes yet), so lint rules and architecture contracts can be protected without locking pyproject.toml. Add both to the guard's _PROTECTED list, the OpenCode/Claude ask rules, and tests/test_agent_permissions.py samples.

Protected via guard (ruff.toml/.ruff.toml at any depth, .importlinter, [tool.ruff in any pyproject.toml), OpenCode and Claude ask rules, test samples. Reviewer PASS; mypy config follow-up amber-7q0.14.

title: Cleanliness harness for agent-driven development
description:
Adapt docs/design/cleanliness-harness-spec.md to amber-nlp, alongside the verification harness (amber-a6d). Enforce what can be measured (complexity, layering, dead code, duplication, dependencies, types, changed-line coverage, suppressions); review what can't (a rubric-driven cleanliness reviewer). New code meets the full standard; legacy code is ratcheted and may not get worse. Agents cannot edit the quality config, baselines, or rubric.

Decisions (2026-11-09): keep mypy and ratchet the mypy --strict error count (no pyright); ADRs in docs/decisions/; split checks by speed (make check and CI run full quality + diff-coverage, the stop hook runs only quality-fast and stays under ~90 s). No Rust core here, so spec section 7 does not apply. Beads replaces the spec's PLAN.md. Reuses amber-a6d's machinery: make targets, protected paths (guard, ask rules, tests/test_agent_permissions.py), ALLOW_ORACLE_CHANGE, hooks, CI labels.

Already present: Ruff (E,F,I,UP,B,SIM), import-linter contracts (core/framework/plugin direction), mypy, the correctness reviewer agent, pytest-cov.
acceptance_criteria: All children closed; the adapted spec section 11 checks pass (verification task).

title: AGENTS.md: definition of done, protected paths, forbidden shortcuts
description: Extend AGENTS.md (CLAUDE.md links to it) per spec section 7, adapted: Definition of done = make check passes and its summary line is quoted in the final message. Protected paths (the single list from the pre-commit task) must not be modified, worked around, or duplicated; if a protected test looks wrong, stop and explain. Forbidden shortcuts: skip/xfail, loosened assertions, special-casing inputs or IDs, swallowing exceptions, editing golden records. Workflow uses Beads acceptance criteria instead of PLAN.md. Keep it concise.
acceptance_criteria: AGENTS.md states the definition of done, protected paths, and forbidden shortcuts; no duplication with CLAUDE.md invariants.
close_reason: AGENTS.md: Definition of done (make check summary quoted; acceptance criteria with evidence; reviewer findings resolved), protected paths (guard script authoritative), forbidden shortcuts, Beads workflow; CLAUDE.md points to it. Reviewer PASS; guard gap filed as a follow-up.

title: Claude Code hooks: post-edit lint/typecheck and stop gate
description: Add .claude/settings.json hooks and .claude/hooks/{post_edit,stop_gate}.py (stdlib only). post_edit: read hook JSON from stdin, for .py under src/ or tests/ run ruff check --fix, ruff format, mypy on the file (or dmypy for speed); errors to stderr, exit 2; must finish in a few seconds. stop_gate: exit 0 if stop_hook_active; exit 0 if git diff --name-only HEAD (plus untracked) shows no src/ or tests/ changes; else run make test-fast and print a one-line summary (N tests passed) or a concise failure list on stderr with exit 2. Verify against current Claude Code hook docs. Do NOT add permission deny rules here (separate task).
acceptance_criteria: A mypy error introduced in an edited file is surfaced by PostToolUse; a failing fast test blocks Stop; stop_hook_active=true does not loop; unit tests for both scripts feed synthetic hook JSON.
close_reason: Claude Code hooks: .claude/settings.json, .claude/hooks/post_edit.py (ruff fix/format; mypy for src/), stop_gate.py (stop_hook_active guard, src/tests change detection incl. untracked, make lint/typecheck/test-fast, exit 2 with failure summary). 26 fake-runner tests; verified live: mypy error surfaced in 0.3 s, failing test blocks stop, active hook exits in 0.05 s.

description: Add a Makefile wrapping the existing uv commands so one command defines done. Targets: lint (ruff check + ruff format --check), typecheck (mypy src), imports (lint-imports), lock (uv lock --check), test-fast (pytest -m 'not slow', target < 60 s; measure and add a marker for slow suites if needed), test (full pytest incl. slow), check (lint typecheck imports lock test-fast), mutation (scripts/mutation_test.py), phi-scan (stub until the scan task lands). Each target prints a one-line summary. Keep scripts thin per scripts/README.md.

close_reason: Makefile added: sync, lint, format, typecheck, imports, lock, test-fast (~40 s), test, check, mutation, help. make check passes (1543 tests, ~45 s). AGENTS.md and tests/README.md point at it. phi-scan target deferred to amber-a6d.3.

description: Add .pre-commit-config.yaml: ruff, ruff-format, mypy (local hook via uv), end-of-file-fixer, trailing-whitespace, check-added-large-files, and a local hook that rejects staged changes to protected paths unless ALLOW_ORACLE_CHANGE=1. Reuse scripts/check_protected_changes.py on the staged diff (git diff --cached --unified=0) so CI and pre-commit share one protected-path list. Extend the list to cover the harness itself: .claude/settings.json, .claude/hooks/**, .opencode harness config, .pre-commit-config.yaml, scripts/check_protected_changes.py, Makefile. This changes the protected-artifact list: follow the contract-change skill; needs the contract-approved label.

PR needs contract-approved.

title: Verification harness for agent-driven development
description:
Adapt docs/design/verification-harness-spec.md to amber-nlp. Verification must be executable, automatic, and outside the agent's control: one command (make check) defines done, agents cannot change the oracle (golden records, catalog, fixtures, test assertions, harness config), and hooks/CI produce the evidence.

Scope decision (2026-11-08): amber owns the guardrails (Makefile, pre-commit, oracle guard, identifier scan, agent hooks and deny rules for Claude Code and OpenCode, AGENTS.md definition of done, reviewer agent, CI wiring) plus a reusable span scorer and regression-gate library. Extraction-quality parts of the spec (behavioral suites for negation/temporality/etc., dev gold, held-out eval, prediction diff) need an extractor and gold data, so per the charter they belong in lapidary and are handed off. Type checking stays on mypy (spec said pyright).

Already present: scripts/check_protected_changes.py + the contract-approved label (spec 9.5), scripts/mutation_test.py (3.6), tests/test_properties.py and the conformance kit (3.2).
acceptance_criteria: All child tasks closed; the adapted spec section 10 checks pass (see the verification task).
close_reason: Verification harness in place on main: make check as definition of done (CI parity), pre-commit + CI guard (oracle, harness, test deselection, text diffs), identifier scan over the whole repo, OpenCode/Claude post-edit + stop hooks, read-only reviewer agent, ask rules on protected paths, pinned OpenCode SDK check, weekly mutation testing, span scorer + regression gate library. Extraction-quality layer handed off to lapidary lap-6ej.

title: Exporter protocol and reference exporter with per-file gating
description: Contract v0.1 sections 6.2 and 6.6 decision 5. Split from amber-bpr.5. Exporter protocol with no fixed payload kind: gate every output file by its schema-derived kind through a PolicyGate, atomic (any refusal writes nothing), ExportReceipt with per-file kind, decision, content_sha256; amber-labels/0.1 holds only labels_only files. Reference exporter over local directories.
acceptance_criteria: IFC-08 with a recording gate; policy refusal writes nothing; round trip through export and re-import.
close_reason: PolicyGate protocol and StaticGate reference; PolicyViolation carries every decision; Exporter protocol with ExportReceipt/ExportedFile; reference LocalExporter (bundles extra) gating every file and the manifest before writing, atomic through a staging directory; amber-labels/0.1 as bundle kind labels (build_labels_bundle, load_labels) holding only labels_only tables and label_records from labels_only_view. IFC-08 covered in tests/test_export.py.

title: Parquet bundles: tables, manifest, content hashes, payload kinds, resolver reader
description: Contract v0.1 sections 5.2, 5.4, 5.5, 5.6. Split from amber-bpr.5. Bundle writer and reader (pyarrow in a new optional extra) for every table; rows sorted by key; content_sha256 over canonical rows and optional file_sha256; payload kinds derived from schemas and answer models; manifest with one dataset and one variable set; resolver-based validation (source_hash_mismatch, source_unavailable) and an unvalidated wrapper refused by the boundaries; x_ columns preserved.
acceptance_criteria: WIR-01 to WIR-13 on synthetic fixtures; the bundle conformance cases (amber-u4c.2) can run.
close_reason: amber.bundles: table schemas, build_bundle (run/gold/review), content_sha256 over key-sorted canonical rows, payload kinds from schemas and answer models, manifest, check_bundle before validation, load_bundle with resolver (text_hash, re-minted spans, results/examples/events/decisions revalidated, examples verified against events) or UnvalidatedBundle refused by boundaries; amber.bundles.parquet write/read with canonical JSON columns, UTC timestamps, file_sha256, x_ columns. New bundles extra (pyarrow). Results and Examples now order records by key. WIR-12 not implemented (noted on amber-u4c.2). Tests in tests/test_bundles.py.

title: JSON record forms: schema_version, budget/usage, VariableSet JSON
description: Contract v0.1 sections 5.2, 5.3, 6.3, 6.6 (decisions 2, 5, 8). Split from amber-bpr.5. schema_version amber/0.1 on CaseResult, Example, AnnotationEvent, LabelRecord, Decision, VariableSet JSON records (reject other majors, accept lower minors); Budget and Usage on CaseResult with the budget check on load (budget_exceeded unless failed(budget)); VariableSet JSON with answer models as JSON Schema plus schema_ref.

close_reason: schema_version amber/0.1 on CaseResult, Example, AnnotationEvent, LabelRecord, Decision, VariableSet JSON (lower minors accepted and normalized, other majors and newer minors rejected); UTC Z six-digit JSON timestamps; Budget/Usage on CaseResult with budget_exceeded unless failed(budget); CaseResult keys in section 5.3 order; amber.wire variable_set_json/load_variable_set; golden JSON fixtures in amber/conformance/golden pinning bytes and keys (WIR-14). Tests in tests/test_wire.py; migration note added.

title: Annotation events, replay to Projection, and Example.from_projection
description: Contract v0.1 sections 4.4, 4.5, 4.10 and 6.2 (Projection). Split from amber-bpr.3. AnnotationEvent (actor and adjudicator validated with parse_producer; role, round, stream, action set, before/after without quotes or offsets, provenance, external_ref); deterministic replay of a case's events up to as_of_event into a Projection that validates under the graph rules; status transitions for claims and readings (corrections are new IDs linked by events; no edit of gold; gold only over gold/verified readings); role-based blind-review visibility; Example.from_projection naming the failing invariant; tier rises only through new events; move-on tier.set by role=system with a decision reference.
acceptance_criteria: Adversarial tests for ANN-04, ANN-06, ANN-07, ANN-09, ANN-10, ANN-15, ANN-18: random event sequences replay identically and prefixes reproduce prefix projections and example_ids; tier asserted without events fails; reviewer stream isolation before resolve.
close_reason: AnnotationEvent; amber.annotations.replay -> Projection (deterministic, prefix-exact, spans resolved from caller records and re-minted); visible_events blind-review rules; status transitions, corrections as new linked records, gold only over reviewed readings; tier rises by role with promotion of finals to gold; move-on tier.set by system with decision_ref; example_from_projection and verify_example (events_mismatch). Graph rule relaxed so rejected claims may feed inferences only rejected claims rely on. Tests in tests/test_annotations.py (ANN-04/06/07/09/10/15/18).

title: Per-variable outcomes and variable_set_ref on CaseResult
description: Contract v0.1 sections 3.5 and 3.10 (decisions 3, 5, 8). VariableOutcome per final variable; CaseResult.outcome and final_claim_ids nullable and equal to the single VariableOutcome for one-variable sets (breaking; record in amber-ndt.6); case_status() by fixed severity order, never stored; mention-level conflicting_evidence rejected; not_mentioned requires declared full review. CaseResult records variable_set, variable_set_version, variable_set_ref; load against a set with a different schema_ref fails with variable_set_mismatch. run_id, budget and usage are out of scope (wire formats).
acceptance_criteria: Adversarial tests for VAR-12, VAR-13 and section 3.10 decision 3 conformance additions; variable_set_mismatch on load.
notes: 2026-11-02 (from amber-hee.1.3): amber.cases refuses variable sets with more than one variable (invalid_context) until VariableOutcome lands; lift it here. Graph snapshots already bind variable_set/version/ref (format 3) and mismatch is invalid_context; results need variable_set_mismatch.
close_reason: VariableOutcome per final variable; CaseResult records variable_set/version/ref; outcome and final_claim_ids mirror the single final variable or are null; case_status by fixed severity; final claims must belong to their variable; mention-level conflicting_evidence refused (invalid_outcome); variable_set_mismatch on load; multi-variable refusal lifted. Migration note added. Tests in tests/test_variable_outcomes.py.

title: Variable-aware claim validation
description: Contract v0.1 sections 2.3 and 3.3. Claim.reading_id (required for mention-level variables, forbidden for note-level); mention-level claim cites its reading's span inclusions, reading not rejected, mention_type in the variable's mention_types; requires_attributes with strict value matching and attribute:<category> edges to exactly the cue (missing_attribute_evidence, attribute_value_not_permitted; lenient accepted); attribute: roles excluded from field coverage; requires_section (citation_outside_section); undeclared_dependency for inference inputs from undeclared variables.
acceptance_criteria: Adversarial tests for MEN-8, MEN-13, MEN-20 and VAR-3 to VAR-7.
notes: 2026-11-02 (from amber-hee.1.3): undeclared_dependency is already enforced for note-level graphs (claims may consume same-variable claims or declared inputs, through nested inferences). build_context currently refuses mention-level variables and requires_section with invalid_context; lift each refusal as its check lands. AttributeRequirement.values is a sorted tuple (not a frozenset) so True and 1 stay distinct; match with strict types.
close_reason: Claim.reading_id (optional field, ULID); mention-level claims need a registered non-rejected reading of a permitted mention_type and must cite its hull or every fragment (uncited_mention); attribute:<category> edges must cite the reading's cue and never count toward field coverage; required attributes with strict-type values (attribute_value_not_permitted, missing_attribute_evidence, lenient); requires_section (citation_outside_section). Graph refusals of mention-level variables and requires_section lifted. Tests in tests/test_mention_claims.py.

title: VariableSet, Variable, and Task as a one-variable set
description: Contract v0.1 sections 3.2 and 3.10 (decisions 7, 8). AttributeRequirement, Variable (level note|mention|patient reserved), VariableSet with validation (unique names, known acyclic inputs, mention-level needs mention_types and no note-level inputs, at least one final) and schema_ref identity (answer models as JSON Schema, version excluded). Task is sugar for a one-variable set; EvidenceGraph accepts task= or variables=; Claim gains variable (breaking; record in amber-ndt.6). Patient level constructible but graphs reject it with invalid_context.
acceptance_criteria: Existing suite passes unchanged through the Task sugar (VAR-1). Adversarial tests for VAR-2 and VAR-15: cycles, unknown inputs, mention-level without types, no final variable, schema_ref changes with any field but not version, patient level rejected by graphs.
close_reason: Variable, VariableSet, AttributeRequirement with set validation and content schema_ref (version excluded); Task sugar via VariableSet.from_task; EvidenceGraph/from_payload/load_case_result accept task= or variables=; Claim.variable; per-variable claim validation and undeclared_dependency; snapshot format 3. Existing suite passes unchanged through the sugar; tests in tests/test_variables.py.

title: MentionReading and attributes in the evidence graph
description: Contract v0.1 sections 2.2-2.3 and 2.9 (decisions 3, 4, 6, 9, 10). Attribute (strict str|bool|int value, cue evidence_id, scope_evidence_id, assigned_by) and MentionReading (ULID, label, value, unit, concept, attributes, inputs, status, provenance). Graph registration order evidence -> mention -> readings; readings resolve mention and attribute evidence; hull inside scope (attribute_outside_scope); assigned_by parsed with parse_producer and never equal to the reading's producer; every mention has a reading. cite(mention) returns hull or fragment inclusions; source_leaves reports mentions and readings at each inclusion. CaseResult carries mentions and mention_readings; cited mentions must be present, uncited ones round-trip.
acceptance_criteria: Adversarial tests for MEN-3, MEN-4, MEN-7, MEN-14, MEN-16, MEN-18, MEN-19 and section 2.9 decision 3 (missing cited mention fails load; uncited mentions round-trip).
notes: 2026-11-02: cite(mention) landed with amber-hee.1.1 (amber.tools.mention.cite). Still here: revalidating Mention payloads at graph registration and load by re-minting through amber.grounding.exact_mention, so a payload whose section_category, fragments, quote, or mention_id disagrees with the authoritative Source is rejected (remaining half of MEN-6).
close_reason: MentionReading, Attribute, Concept; register_mention/register_reading with reading, cue/scope, attribute_outside_scope, and status checks; mention payloads re-minted on load (MEN-6); mentions_at/readings_of; graph snapshot v2 and CaseResult mentions + mention_readings with migration note. Tests in tests/test_mention_readings.py.

title: Mention span and mention() tool
description: Contract v0.1 sections 2.2 and 2.9 (decisions 5, 7, 8). Mention model (span: source_id, start, end, quote, mention_type, fragments, section_category) minted only by a mention() tool beside quote(), under the same guard as Inclusion. mention_id hashes fragments only when nonempty; contiguous IDs unchanged. section_category derived from Source.sections. Remove Inclusion.mention_id (breaking; record in amber-ndt.6).

Unicode and CRLF offsets.

Tests in tests/test_mentions.py and test_graph_validation.py; load-time Mention revalidation deferred to amber-hee.1.2.

New amber.ids.parse_producer validates rule:/model:/human:/tool: references; Provenance.producer, Attribute.assigned_by, AnnotationEvent.actor, and VariableReference annotators/adjudicator use it. self_reference comparison strips the rule +hash. Provenance gains destination, policy_version, restriction_ids (breaking).

Models not yet built (Attribute, AnnotationEvent, VariableReference) noted on amber-hee.1 and amber-bpr.3.

Keep note scope; patient-level aggregation stays deferred but must not be precluded. Timebox: decide the shapes that bpr.2/bpr.3/bpr.4 must not preclude.

title: Decide CaseOutcome mapping for rule-set abstain vs silent outputs
description: Compiled clinical IE design (docs/design/compiled-clinical-ie.md §6.2, §12 item 1) proposes: explicit rule abstain maps to insufficient_evidence or conflicting_evidence citing the triggering inclusion; silent (no target found) maps to not_mentioned only under a task protocol accepting rule-based whole-note coverage, else the Labeler records no reference. Confirm against contract v0.1 outcome and Labeler rules, or amend. Relates to amber-0z4.2.
close_reason: Decided (user accepted proposal 2026-11-04): abstain -> insufficient_evidence citing the trigger; disagreeing values -> conflicting_evidence at note level only; silent -> not_mentioned only under declared whole-note coverage, else insufficient_evidence (extractor) or LabelerFailure (labeler). Recorded in docs/design/compiled-clinical-ie.md §6.2/§12; tests come with the copal adapter.

comments.author: Will Thompson
comments.text: Proposal (for decision): confirm the §6.2 mapping with three refinements, no contract change. (1) Abstain (target found, cannot decide) -> insufficient_evidence with the reason code in reason and evidence_ids citing the triggering inclusion (CaseOutcome already allows cited evidence on any non-answer; _validate_outcome checks it is source-leaf evidence). Two disagreeing values -> conflicting_evidence citing both, at note level only; at mention level conflicting_evidence is invalid (VAR-14), so a mention-level abstain is always insufficient_evidence. (2) Silent on an Extractor result -> not_mentioned only when the rule set declares whole-note coverage (reviewed_source_ids = the case's sources, which _validate_outcome requires); otherwise insufficient_evidence with reviewed_source_ids empty, matching decision 3 for mention level (zero claims without full review). Evaluation then counts it in O (omission), and a silent output on a target-bearing note is a false negative only under declared coverage. (3) Silent from a Labeler (references) without declared coverage -> LabelerFailure (no reference), never a silver not_mentioned. The coverage declaration belongs to the copal adapter's rule-set configuration (e.g. whole_note_coverage: true, recorded in provenance), not the contract. Follow-up when the copal adapter exists: tests for the three mappings.
